title: Lateral Sell Pocket Heuristics (draft)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, low-friction pocket guide for SEs and AEs to land "lateral" expansion opportunities inside accounts where a purchasing decision is not yet centered on inference (e.g., product teams, embedded platform teams, or data infra). Target: 3-5 minute seller vignettes + 1 slide

Audience:
- Field SEs (mid-to-senior)
- Account Execs running pilot conversations
- Platform / integrator partners prepping a short call

Status / how to use this doc:
- Rough pocketbook: paste into mobile notes or SE cheat-sheet.
- Each play = 1 minute opening + 2 minute demo/case + 1 next-step ask.
- This is intentionally terse — follow-up collateral links at bottom.

Core heuristic (one-liner):
Find a small, well-scoped path to demonstrable value where latency/economics matter but model fidelity can be traded using fallbacks (cache / rerank / cheaper variant). Sell the velocity to ship a pilot, not the final architecture.

Play 1: UX-Speed Win ("Make search stop waiting")
Trigger signals:
- Customer complaint: search results are slow or p95 latency high
- Product manager wants faster time-to-first-answer

1-min opener: "We can get sub-200ms first answer for many embedded search flows by routing queries to a low-latency variant + prefix cache. We do this without touching your model training or data pipeline — short pilot, measurable SLA."

Demo sketch (2 min):
- Slide: p99 latency baseline (customer) -> projected with Redwood runtime
- Quick script: show sample query, show timing delta (60-350ms -> 120ms).
- Highlight fallbacks: quantized variant, prefix cache, local KV for hot queries.
Next-step ask: "Run a 7-day pilot on a subset of queries (10k/day). I'll put together a config and a cost estimate."

Objections & short responses:
- "We can't risk hallucinations" -> "Pilot focuses on highly structured search; we can enable strong reranking and exact-match fallbacks."
- "Cost" -> "We'll pilot on a scoped subset and instrument token-level cost — we can gate traffic if unit cost runs hot."

Play 2: Platform Integrator Proof ("Embed with predictable economics")
Trigger signals:
- Platform team building an integration/marketplace
- Concerned about multi-tenant cost spikes or unpredictable latency

1-min opener: "We'll create a small, dedicated route for partner traffic with reserved capacity and deterministic cost per 1k queries. That gives you a reproducible SLA to promise your partners while we optimize batch/caching."

Demo sketch (2 min):
- Show config: routing policy -> dedicated pool -> canary rollback -> cost cap alerts.
- Show example: partner X onboards with reserved qps 50, autoscale burst 200. Cost sheet snapshot.
Next-step ask: "Agree to a pilot statement of work (2-week scope) and sizing call with infra to lock a reserve."

Play 3: Compliance-First Micropilot ("Bring data to us safely")
Trigger signals:
- Legal / security asks about data residency, KMS, audit logs

1-min opener: "We can spin a Private route in a VPC, keep logs in your KMS, and deliver an audit log for a narrow dataset. That avoids sharing raw customer data with hosted models while you validate results."

Demo sketch (2 min):
- Outline required items: IP allowlist, KMS ARN, retention window.
- Show quick checklist to run a POC in staging.
Next-step ask: "Security handoff to run a short compliance checklist; timeline: 1-2 weeks."

Rapid objection map (bullet answers, keep in pocket):
- "We need on-prem only" -> "We support private deployment and an on-prem package; for pilots, the VPC private control plane is usually faster to validate."
- "We need model explainability" -> "We pair deterministic rerankers/structured outputs so you can show supervised steps in each response."

Metrics to track during pilot (keep as watchlist):
- p50/p95/p99 latency by route
- tokens per response (avg) and tokens per user-session
- cost per 1k queries (projected vs actual)
- quality hit rate (manual eval on 50 samples/day)
- failure rate / fallback %

Short scripts (one-liners for SE to say verbatim):
- "Let's run a scoped pilot on a single route for two weeks — we instrument cost + quality and we'll meet weekly with your PM."
- "If latency is the constraint, we can route to a lower-cost variant while keeping your golden path on a canary."

Roleplay prompts (2-min practice for SEs):
- AE: "We get lots of queries, but it's expensive."
- SE: "Which 10% of queries are the most important? Let's scope those for a pilot. We'll instrument and share a dashboard by day 3."

Deck outline (single slide each, 6-slide mini-deck):
1) Hook + outcome (what customer gets in 2 weeks)
2) Signals that justify a pilot (data points to collect)
3) Technical approach (routes, caches, fallbacks)
4) Cost / capacity snapshot (expected range)
5) Risk controls (canary, rollback, auditing)
6) Next steps + contact / SOW ask

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need sample cost table for 10k / 50k / 200k queries (ask pricing ops for updated unit tiers).
- Validate the replicable demo script with a real customer baseline (ask Jonah to pull 3 anonymized examples).
- Decide if we include a 1-click Helm + config snippet for SEs to provision quick demos (engineering time needed).

Supporting links (quick):
- internal notes: CONFLUENCE-4321 (lateral-sell-evidence)
- pilot SOW template: github.com/redwood-inference/templates/pilot-sow.md
- routing policy primer (internal deck): CONFLUENCE-8812

Appendix: quick checklist for kickoff (copy into calendar invite)
- scope: user flows, sample queries (50), success criteria (latency threshold, cost cap)
- roles: AE owner, SE technical lead, infra contact, security reviewer
- timeline: day 0 kickoff, day 3 demo/dashboard, day 7 mid-check, day 14 wrap + go/no-go

Notes to self (marisol):
- Keep language minimal — this is a pocket heuristic doc for quick memory recall.
- Iterate with field feedback next month (run 3 pilots, gather notes).
- Potentially convert to 2-slide rapid-play card for Sales enablement app.
content_short: Pocket heuristics for quick pilot plays that address latency/cost friction and deliver measurable outcomes in 2 weeks. Three plays: UX-Speed Win, Platform Integrator Proof, Compliance-First Micropilot. Includes one-liners, demo sketches, objections, metrics, and kickoff checklist.
